status: paper exercise - nothing published, nothing mailed, no live list touched

headline.primary_label: Value of a flat +5% on the in-scope base
headline.collectable_label: Collectable once lines with no move available are excluded
headline.note: Both figures are reported with equal weight. A single flat rate makes the euro-weighted move equal the rate itself. The collectable figure is the one that lands as money; the larger figure is the arithmetic on the whole in-scope base and must not be quoted as cash.

movability.mask_note: A line can take a new price only if it already carries a price on both sides of the revision. This is the same mask the pricing policy paper uses when it states 47,617 lines / EUR 32,595,852.63 / 93.15% of billed.
movability.not_a_no_list_claim: This is not the CY2025 no-list gap of 522 part numbers / EUR 4.96M that the pricing policy paper records. That figure is a different window (CY2025) and a different mask, and it is not used here. The immovable set on this basis is the unpriced residual the paper states for this window: EUR 2,397,756.76.
movability.superseded_error: An earlier build of this page reported 1,647 lines / EUR 4.48M immovable, using `value_eur_step != 0` as the test. That wrongly excluded 611 lines that carry a price on both sides but did not move in the last revision (EUR 2,085,484.90). Corrected 2026-09-17.

published_headline.basis: quantity-weighted base-price move on the movable set
published_headline.source: 01_data/90_INBOX/PRICING_POLICY_PAPER_2026-09-17.md - stated as the headline in section 1 and confirmed in the AIM priority-list handoff

simulation_quantity.basis: weighted on the simulation's own quantity rather than billed quantity

euro_weighted.basis: each line's move weighted by the euro it billed
euro_weighted.source: recomputed here; the paper names the two bases above and not this one

step_on_priced_volume.basis: value_eur_step divided by billed euro on the movable set

versus_existing_revision.rate_note: There is no second reconciliation story. The published 5.9616% is the quantity-weighted base-price move and it ties to the published step to the cent. The two sensitivities the paper already documents are 6.06% (simulation quantity) and 5.068% (step on priced volume), and both reproduce on this file. An earlier build of this page reported 5.9787% and 6.2347% on the wrong masks and claimed the published rate had an unreproducible denominator. That claim was unsupported and has been withdrawn.
versus_existing_revision.note: Both are measured on the in-scope L12M base. They are two separate proposals, not two components of one increase.

fx_fork_open.note: A 163.7 -> 172.6 move cuts our euro purchase cost by about 5.2%, which is approximately the size of this entire increase. Settling this before the list is built is Jerome's call and is deliberately left open.

memo_cross_check.note: Illustrative +5% euro on the forecast-weight basis. A different base from the in-scope revision base above; do not add the two.

caveats: No volume response is modelled. No elasticity coefficient exists in this workspace.
The billing extract carries net value only - no gross, discount or condition.
AIM level 1 covers less than the whole book; the remainder is shown explicitly.
Lines with no base price on one side cannot take a new price, so their euro is not collectable by pricing. They are counted and labelled, never dropped.
The collectable figure is the one that lands as money. The all-in-scope figure is whole-base arithmetic and must not be quoted as cash.
The CY2025 no-list gap of 522 part numbers / EUR 4.96M is a different window and is not used anywhere on this page.
This is a paper exercise on the current list. Nothing was published, nothing was mailed, and no live list was touched.
